archetypes.name: callsite-gap-audit
archetypes.rationale: The issue enumerates ~30 specific network-touching callsites across Tier 1/2/3; the plan must wrap every one — any miss ships with the original vulnerability
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-reference every callsite named in the issue's Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 audit against the plan's per-file wrapping sections. Flag any callsite present in the issue audit that is absent from the plan's per-file change sections. Pay special attention to `gh pr edit` at `scripts/ship-pr.sh:1622` and `scripts/ship-pr.sh:2761`, which the issue lists as Tier 1 gaps but the plan's ship-pr.sh section only updates 'existing internal callsites' that already call `with_transient_retry` — verify whether those two `gh pr edit` lines are wrapped or silently left bare. Also verify the plan's claim of '7 existing internal callsites' in ship-pr.sh against the actual callsite list: the plan enumerates lines 1549, 1556, 1585, 1592, 2891, 3087, 3266 but omits any mention of line 3067 in the numbered list despite a parenthetical reference to it elsewhere. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: global-state-contract
archetypes.rationale: _WTR_OUT and _WTR_RC are process-global variables reset on every with_transient_retry entry; scripts with multiple successive wraps must capture them before the next call or risk silent result corruption
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the plan's canonical call pattern — allocate fail_file with mktemp, call with_transient_retry, then read _WTR_OUT and _WTR_RC — and verify that every per-file plan section that wraps multiple callsites captures _WTR_RC into a local variable before the next with_transient_retry call can overwrite it. Identify plan sections that describe multiple successive wraps in the same script branch (e.g., tracking-issue-write.sh lines 481 and 534, merge-pr.sh lines 281 and 318, design-log-publish.sh lines 610, 628, and 657) and check whether the plan's prose or code shows a capture-before-next-call discipline or leaves the clobber hazard implicit. Also verify that the plan's fail_file mktemp allocation requirement is stated for each new callsite, since the helper truncates the file at the start of every attempt and a reused fail_file variable from a prior call would silently receive stale error output on partial-failure branches. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: wrapper-rename-regression
archetypes.rationale: Renaming ship-pr.sh's local with_transient_retry to ship_pr_with_transient_retry is a mechanical rename across 8 internal callsites; the thin wrapper must exactly preserve predicate-before-rc=0 ordering that the merge_pr and ci_wait predicates depend on
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan's proposed ship_pr_with_transient_retry thin wrapper preserves the original helper's control flow: the custom predicate runs against the captured envelope before the rc=0 short-circuit, so an rc=0 response that still triggers transient_envelope_predicate_merge_pr or transient_envelope_predicate_ci_wait will still retry. Confirm the plan's wrapper code actually delegates the predicate call to the lifted lib-net.sh helper rather than re-implementing the check after the helper returns. Check whether the plan accounts for the 8th ship-pr.sh callsite at line 3067 (which uses transient_envelope_predicate_ci_wait, not _none) — the plan's explicit 7-callsite list omits it, creating a risk that line 3067 is left calling the deleted local definition. Also verify that the plan addresses the LARCH_LIB_NET_LOADED guard interaction: if a script sources lib-net.sh and the new with_transient_retry is protected by that guard, a script that was already sourcing lib-net.sh before the change will silently skip loading the new function unless the guard is cleared or the function is defined outside the guard block. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
